subsystems.name: Discretisation and system assembly
subsystems.role: turns a differential equation into the finite algebraic problem a quantum computer can actually act on.
parts: linear or linearised ODE/PDE system Ax = b

subsystems.name: Block encoding
subsystems.role: exposes the system matrix to the quantum computer as a unitary it can call, without ever writing the whole matrix out.

subsystems.name: State preparation
subsystems.role: loads the initial and boundary data as a quantum state vector.
parts: amplitude-encoding circuit or quantum random-access memory

subsystems.name: Solver core
subsystems.role: produces a state whose amplitudes encode the solution.
parts: quantum linear-ODE integrators (Taylor or Chebyshev series)
or variational ansatz with a classical optimiser

subsystems.name: Readout and post-processing
subsystems.role: extracts the handful of physical numbers a user actually wants from the solution state.

subsystems.name: Error mitigation and verification
subsystems.role: keeps shallow-circuit results meaningful and checks them against known classical answers.
parts: classical reference solvers on small instances

buildSteps.title: Pick a regime where classical solvers hurt
buildSteps.detail: Target three-dimensional, high-resolution or many-query problems where classical cost grows steeply, rather than problems a laptop already handles.

buildSteps.title: Discretise the equation
buildSteps.detail: Apply finite differences or finite elements on a grid, obtaining a large sparse linear system, and record its condition number and dimension.

buildSteps.title: Estimate the resources honestly
buildSteps.detail: Before building anything, count qubits, gate depth and readout shots against the best classical method for the same instance.

buildSteps.title: Block-encode the operator
buildSteps.detail: Construct circuits that apply the system matrix as a unitary, using a sparse oracle or a sum of simple unitaries, at fault-tolerant precision.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the input state
buildSteps.detail: Encode the source term or initial condition into amplitudes — typically the most expensive and least efficient part of the pipeline.

buildSteps.title: Run the solver
buildSteps.detail: Either execute the deep linear-systems or time-stepping circuit on an error-corrected machine, or optimise a shallow variational circuit on today's hardware for toy sizes.

buildSteps.title: Extract physical quantities
buildSteps.detail: Sample the output state to estimate the specific integrals, fluxes or prices wanted; a full solution field cannot be read out cheaply.

buildSteps.title: Verify and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Compare against a classical solver on small grids, apply error mitigation, and only then scale the problem size.

buildSteps.title: Quantify the advantage
buildSteps.detail: State clearly which quantity is faster, under what precision and conditioning assumptions, and check that a classical or 'dequantised' method cannot match it.

prerequisites.tech: Fault-tolerant quantum computing with error correction
prerequisites.why: the needed circuit depths and precisions are far beyond today's noisy devices.
demonstrated on small systems; the cost still grows with matrix size and precision.

prerequisites.tech: Efficient quantum state preparation and quantum memory
prerequisites.why: loading arbitrary initial data can be as costly as the problem being solved.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum observable estimation and amplitude estimation
prerequisites.why: the solution exists as amplitudes; only aggregate quantities can be read out efficiently.

prerequisites.tech: Mature classical PDE and Monte Carlo solvers as the benchmark
prerequisites.why: the bar to beat is high and improves every year, so any advantage must be measured against it.

pathway.milestone: Small demonstrations on tens of qubits: variational solvers for simple ODEs and low-dimensional PDEs, plus theory papers giving end-to-end complexity for linear equations
pathway.unlocks: proof that the pipeline runs, and a clear list of bottlenecks — state preparation, conditioning and readout.

pathway.milestone: Fault-tolerant proof-of-concept solving an instance chosen so that a specific quantity is certifiably hard to compute classically
pathway.unlocks: first credible claim of an equation-solving advantage on a narrow problem class.

pathway.milestone: Application-specific routines for electromagnetics, option pricing and linearised flow, exploiting structure such as low rank, sparsity or many repeated solves
pathway.unlocks: early commercial use inside larger classical workflows, where only a small subproblem is quantum.

pathway.milestone: Fault-tolerant machines with enough logical qubits for practical grids
pathway.unlocks: nonlinear and turbulent flow simulation, where independent classical verification is hardest.
